clue.text: 11A's tip on National horse going around band of miscreants

indicators.note: the horse's letters go around the other two, enclosing them

parts.note: a gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next
the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the clue at 11 across, a king of legend

explanation.surface: A Grand National runner circles a crowd of troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National horse' looks like one racing phrase; N and the horse split. 11A is ARTHUR, so its tip is A.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a band of miscreants is a criminal mob or crew.

clue.text: Support helping jockey to move radius fully

parts.note: to stir is to move or budge
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry
up can mean completely, as in eat up or use up

explanation.surface: Something that helps a rider shift fully along a bone of the forearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the foot loop hanging from a saddle supports the rider.

clue.text: Scrooge, latest part for Alastair Sim, incorporating 10 finally growing up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, growing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
incorporating means taking another piece inside
the latest part of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the actor's surname gives the letters

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter

parts.note: the clue at 10 across, the actor George's surname

explanation.surface: A question whether Alastair Sim's newest role was a growing-up Scrooge.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastair Sim famously played Scrooge in the 1951 film, so the surface is a trap. R and SIM take in E, the last letter of 10's COLE, and the whole is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym: Dickens's Scrooge is the archetype of a hoarding skinflint.

clue.text: Arm 6's women residents?

parts.note: in means at home, residing
the clue at 6 across, Deva, is the Roman name of Chester

explanation.surface: Asking what the women who live in a certain city are called.
explanation.walkthrough: Women in the city of 6 (Deva, the Roman name for Chester) reads W IN CHESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Winchester is a famous make of rifle, a firearm.

clue.text: Not being watchful, model Renault left on back of lorry

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new order
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A Renault model, left on the tail of a lorry, carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like part of the car description but signals an anagram of RENAULT plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: acting without alertness is acting inattentively.

clue.text: Good spirit in "home-made" VAT Dave's mixed

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the name are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the name Dave, with 's read as is; the same letters also lie hidden in 'home-made VAT', a deliberate second route, not a coincidence

explanation.surface: A homemade brew stirred up in a vat by Dave.
explanation.walkthrough: Double wordplay: the letters also run hidden across 'made VAT', with 'in' as the signal. Dave is the barman in Minder.
explanation.definitionFit: A deva is a benevolent divine being in Hindu and Buddhist belief.

clue.text: The World that was St Patrick's Lobster, innovatively serialised?

definitions.text: The World that was St Patrick's

indicators.note: serialised suggests letters run on from one word into the next, so the answer is lodged across them

explanation.surface: A seafood dish, served up in instalments, from St Patrick's old world.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Lobster' and the start of 'innovatively'; 'Er Indoors is also Arthur Daley's name for his wife in Minder.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic name: this old name for Ireland was the whole world to the island's patron saint.

clue.text: Here there's instant suffering involving tormented Sir

indicators.note: suffering describes the word instant as distressed, so its letters are disturbed
tormented describes Sir as twisted about, so its letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A place where instant misery engulfs a tortured knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' points to the girls' school of the films, famous for its anarchic pupils; 'involving' joins the two jumbled words into one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-referential: the infamous school is where the torment goes on, so it is the place referred to.

clue.text: Got clean carried away

definitions.meaning: taken along by a strong force, as by a crowd

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: brushed tidy, and swept along by something forceful.

clue.text: Chase stock car, finally stopping self-drive on Westway?

parts.note: kin is stock, as in family or lineage

indicators.note: heading west on the road means travelling right to left, so the letters are read backwards in this across entry
stopping means plugging a gap, so the car's last letter sits inside

parts.note: the ego is the self

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter

parts.note: to egg on is to drive or urge forward

explanation.surface: A pursuit around a car-racing track, a hire car stopped on a London motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Westway is an elevated road in west London; 'on Westway?' turns the self-and-drive pieces round, as traffic heading west in an across entry runs right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the King George VI Chase is a famous steeplechase run at Kempton Park on Boxing Day.

clue.text: An item that's cutting up cabbage

indicators.note: cutting means removing the following word's letters from within

parts.note: a couple who are romantically linked are said to be an item
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that chops cabbage, such as a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting up' looks like chopping; it says UP is cut from COUPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical name: cole is an old general word for brassicas such as kale and cabbage.

clue.text: Old King Henry the Fifth of England right to advance on old city

indicators.note: picks the fifth letter of the following word

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: King Henry V of England advancing on an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old King Henry the Fifth' reads as one monarch; the king is the definition, and 'right to advance' puts A and RT ahead of H.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the legendary ruler of Camelot is an ancient British monarch.

clue.text: Extended action with smasher after a week's a bit hard to deal with

definitions.text: a bit hard to deal with

indicators.note: after places the action and smasher behind the preceding pieces

parts.note: a war is a prolonged military action
a dish is slang for an attractive person, a smasher

explanation.surface: A long campaign with a heavy hitter after a week proves tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: somewhat difficult to manage is somewhat clumsy or tricky.

clue.text: Shakespearean actress makes effort to take in bestower of OBEs

indicators.note: to take in means to hold another piece inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt or effort
ER, the Queen, confers honours such as the OBE

explanation.surface: An actress strives to embrace the person who hands out honours.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Ellen Terry was a celebrated Victorian player of Shakespeare's heroines.

clue.text: New wives carried over them, making Bliss drool horribly (bachelor no more!)

indicators.note: horribly describes the letters as badly jumbled
no more says the bachelor's letter is gone from the mix

explanation.surface: A groom drools over wedded bliss, no longer a single man.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B from BLISS DROOL and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: brides are traditionally carried across the threshold strips of their new homes.

clue.text: Secure with Penny, the country 10 nearly backed

indicators.note: backed means the run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

indicators.note: nearly drops the final letter

parts.note: the clue at 10 across, the actor George's surname

explanation.surface: Supporting a national figure with a penny, reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is the actor George Cole, so 'nearly' trims his surname before everything is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to secure something is to fasten it away behind a key.

clue.text: Mini's label initially switched after pound sign

indicators.note: after puts the pound sign in front of the switched label

parts.note: L is the sign for a pound, as in the pound sterling

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word swap places

parts.note: a title is a label or heading

explanation.surface: A car's badge has its first letters swapped after a pound sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mini' looks like the car; it is the adjective meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something mini is small or tiny.

clue.text: It's not brief handling hot crook gently

indicators.note: handling means holding another piece in its grasp
crook as an adjective means bent or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A crook gently handles hot goods, and it takes a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a villain but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation of a synonym: the opposite of short or concise is long-winded.

clue.text: Stock-in-trade of used-car salesman causing fireworks

definitions.meaning: old, worn-out cars, the goods a dodgy dealer sells

explanation.surface: A shady car dealer's stock goes off with a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for old rattling cars, and the noisy fireworks that go off with a report.

clue.text: Line crossed by Comrade Dad centrally following "Advance" order

indicators.note: following places the line part after the opening letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advance

indicators.note: crossed by means the line is cut through by the inner letters

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

indicators.note: centrally picks the middle letter of each word

explanation.surface: A line of comrades and dads obeys a march order.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an array is an ordered arrangement or display.

clue.text: He's paid attention in the end to departing expert

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: departing means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a oner is an expert, someone unique at something

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone who has listened at last to a retiring specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's paid attention' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'paid'. ONER loses O, the end of 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a wage earner is someone who receives pay for working.

clue.text: The Bill on the case of his undrinkable spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue the police sit on top of the rest

parts.note: the Bill is slang for the police, here the Met, London's force

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: The police find his undrinkable liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MET is London's Metropolitan Police, the Old Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Methylated spirits is denatured alcohol, deliberately made unfit to drink.

clue.text: The wife's endless deceit

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: fraud is deceit or swindling

explanation.surface: A wife's lies have no limit.
explanation.definitionFit: German usage: a German wife, or Mrs, is called by this title.

clue.text: Sanity of Chisholm in doubt

indicators.note: of says the letters come out from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Questioning a man named Chisholm's mental state.
explanation.walkthrough: Chisholm is the police sergeant in Minder.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to be in one's right mind is to be sane.

clue.text: They look like workers getting busy to arrange set

indicators.note: getting busy means the letters are set to work and moved about

explanation.surface: Some people hard at work organise a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' sounds like people but means worker ants.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoological term: these are ants of a reproductive caste that resemble worker ants.

clue.text: One tip or the other from Waterman: "I could be so good for you"

indicators.note: a tip is an end letter, here the final one
the other tip is the opening letter
from takes the second, and closing, letter of this two-letter word, completing the run of tips

explanation.surface: Dennis Waterman sings the Minder theme, 'I Could Be So Good for You'.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word gives one end, first or last: the N of Waterman, I itself, the C of could, the E of be.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something nice is pleasant or good.

clue.text: Spiv, young, holding whip hand? Half right

indicators.note: holding means the young fish wrap round the rest

parts.note: fry are young fish
a lash is a whip

indicators.note: half of the word hand gives its first two letters

explanation.surface: A wide boy, still young, gets the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Flash Harry was the spiv in the St Trinian's films, played by George Cole.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the character is the classic flashy wide boy dealing in black-market goods.

clue.text: Throw into confusion the seeds of campaign (Lynchwood underestimating Blott!)

indicators.note: the seeds of words are their first letters, from which they grow

explanation.surface: A campaign is thrown into disarray when Lynchwood underrates Blott.
explanation.walkthrough: A rare military sense: to club troops is to muddle their formation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary sense: in old military usage, to club a body of soldiers is to throw it into disorder.
